subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Range Anxiety
description: A fast breakdown of Range Anxiety for builders.

hook.text: The fear of running out of charge before reaching a charger has a name: range anxiety.

buildup.text: Early EVs with 80-mile range made this fear very real. A wrong turn could mean a tow truck.

discovery.text: Modern EVs offer 250–400 miles per charge. Most Americans drive under 40 miles a day.

twist.text: Studies show people overestimate how much range they need. The anxiety is often psychological, not practical.

climax.text: Better charging networks are erasing the last real gaps. Range anxiety is fading each year.

punchline.text: Most EV owners forget range anxiety within months.

quiz.question: How far does the average American drive daily?

details.summary: Range anxiety is the fear that an EV's battery will run out before reaching a charger, a psychological barrier that persists even as modern EVs offer 300-plus miles of range and charging networks expand.
details.whyItMatters: Range anxiety remains the top reason consumers hesitate to buy EVs, despite most daily driving being well within current battery capacity. Overcoming this perception is crucial for mass adoption.
takeaways: Most Americans drive fewer than 40 miles per day on average
Modern EVs offer 250 to 400 miles of range per charge
Visible charging infrastructure reduces range anxiety significantly

faq.question: Is range anxiety justified with today's EVs?
faq.answer: For daily driving, no. Most EVs far exceed typical daily mileage. For long road trips, some planning is still needed, but fast-charging networks are expanding rapidly. The anxiety is increasingly psychological rather than practical.

faq.question: What range do most EV buyers actually need?
faq.answer: Studies show 200 miles of range covers 99 percent of daily driving needs. Buyers overestimate their range requirements because they plan for rare worst-case trips rather than typical daily use.
